With the completion of the Jesus Christ tower, the tallest of 18 in the temple, the basilica has reached its full height of 172.5 metres. It is now not only the world’s tallest church but Barcelona’s tallest building. It was consecrated in 2010 by Pope Benedict XVI.

The blessing arrives on the centenary of the monument's architect Antoni Gaudí. by Richard Whiddington June 10, 2026 ShareShare This Article Pope Leo XIV arrived in Barcelona, Spain, on June 10 to bless the new tower of the Sagrada Familia Basilica. In a widely hailed development, the central Tower of Jesus Christ was completed in February, bringing the Basilica’s height up to up 566 feet and earning the structure the designation of world’s tallest church. Now, the leader of the Catholic Church will hold mass inside the modernist landmark on the 100th anniversary of the death of its architect Antoni Gaudí. The inauguration is being live-streamed on TikTok, as well as the Sagrada Familia’s website, and will see more than 8,000 people gather before the pontiff, including Spain’s prime minister Pedro Sanchez.

The Spanish king and queen traveled to Barcelona on Wednesday to join Pope Leo for a historic mass, marking the symbolic completion of one of the world’s most recognized buildings. Pope Leo blessed the 18th and final completed tower at Barcelona’s Sagrada Família on the centennial of architect Antoni Gaudí's death, 144 years after construction first began at the site.

original_article.research:
[Lähde: The Guardian World]
As completion of 144-year basilica nears, questions swirl over resemblance of church to architect’s original plans

It has been a long wait but 144 years after work began, Pope Leo XIV has blessed the recently completed central tower of Antoni Gaudí’s Sagrada Família church in the presence of members of the Spanish royal family, the prime minister and hundreds of bishops.

With the completion of the Jesus Christ tower, the tallest of 18 in the temple, the basilica has reached its full height of 172.5 metres. It is now not only the world’s tallest church but Barcelona’s tallest building. It was consecrated in 2010 by Pope Benedict XVI.

After a solemn Mass, the Pope, speaking in Spanish and Catalan, said that, more than a monument, “this basilica is a work in progress, which reminds us that the path that Christ has shown us is a journey that never ends”. He added: “We can never believe is a Jesus that wants us to make war or murder innocents.”

Before Wednesday’s service, Leo lit a candle and prayed at the tomb of Gaudí in the basilica’s crypt.

Ten hours before he was due to pass by, the faithful were already picking their spots along the pope’s route.

Ramón and Marisa from L’Hospitalet de Llobregat, both draped in Vatican flags, were among those who had arrived early to drink in the atmosphere. “We’re of the generation of John Paul II and Leo reminds us a lot of him,” Marisa said. “We’re very happy that he’s come here to Barcelona.”

Ramón said the Sagrada Família gives him goosebumps. “Gaudí deserves to be a saint just for building it,” Marisa said. “It’s a divine construction.”

A few blocks away, Rosmira Pasadis from Venezuela said she’d brought some fruit and water to get her through the long wait.

“This pope is very charismatic and he’s got a gift for communicating, especially with the young,” she said. “His visit is important for me not just because I’m a Catholic but because we hope he will call for the release of political prisoners in Venezuela and for our freedom.”

Security measures, which include the closure of several metro stations and streets, brought the city close to a standstill, while only invited guests can get anywhere near the Sagrada Família itself.

However, souvenir shops nearby were doing steady business selling pope memorabilia alongside their usual collection of Gaudiana tat.

The blessing arrives on the centenary of the monument's architect Antoni Gaudí.

by 
                                                                                                    Richard Whiddington  
                                                                                                June 10, 2026
                                                
                                                

     ShareShare This Article

Pope Leo XIV arrived in Barcelona, Spain, on June 10 to bless the new tower of the Sagrada Familia Basilica.

In a widely hailed development, the central Tower of Jesus Christ was completed in February, bringing the Basilica’s height up to up 566 feet and earning the structure the designation of world’s tallest church. Now, the leader of the Catholic Church will hold mass inside the modernist landmark on the 100th anniversary of the death of its architect Antoni Gaudí.

The inauguration is being live-streamed on TikTok, as well as the Sagrada Familia’s website, and will see more than 8,000 people gather before the pontiff, including Spain’s prime minister Pedro Sanchez.

Pope Leo XIV greets faithful as he presides over the Midday Prayer at the Cathedral of the Holy Cross and Saint Eulalia in Barcelona. Photo: Simone Risoluti/Vatican Media via Vatican Pool/Getty Images.

Gaudí was a devout Catholic who died at the age of 73 after being hit by a tram while on his way to church. The Sagrada Familia is duly packed with depictions of religious figures and Biblical scenes and its central spire falls short of Barcelona’s Montjuic hill in respect for God. Such piety has long seen Gaudí labelled “God’s architect,” but in recent years the Vatican has hinted it may canonize him as a saint.

When Pope Benedict XVI consecrated the Sagrada Familia in 2010, he described Gaudí as “a practicing Christian who kept the torch of his faith alight to the end of his life.” In 2025, Pope Francis recognized Gaudí for his “heroic virtues,” the second in a four-step process towards being recognized as a saint by the Catholic Church. Steps three and four require verifiable miracles being attributed to the architect. The Archdiocese of Barcelona has been putting Gaudí’s case before the Vatican since 2023. Accordingly, Pope Leo’s words and actions will be closely watched.

Pope Leo XIV walks under a processional canopy following the Holy Mass held in the Plaza de Cibeles in Madrid. Photo: Getty Images.

Pope Leo blessed the 18th and final completed tower at Barcelona’s Sagrada Família on the centennial of architect Antoni Gaudí's death, 144 years after construction first began at the site.

Gaudí began reimagining the project in 1883, a year after construction first broke ground under a different architect. He died in 1926, struck by a streetcar in Barcelona, with only a fraction of the work complete. The Spanish Civil War halted construction for years, and anarchist groups destroyed many of his original plans and models. payload.title: Paavi siunasi Sagrada Famílian viimeisen tornin Barcelonassa
payload.summary: Paavi Leo XIV on siunannut Sagrada Famílian uuden keskustornin Barcelonassa. Jeesuksen Kristuksen tornin valmistuminen nostaa Antoni Gaudín suunnitteleman basilikan 172,5 metrin korkeuteen ja tekee siitä maailman korkeimman kirkon.
payload.content:
Paavi Leo XIV on siunannut Barcelonassa Sagrada Famílian hiljattain valmistuneen keskustornin, kun 144 vuotta rakenteilla ollut basilika lähestyy symbolista valmistumistaan. Jeesuksen Kristuksen torni on rakennuksen 18 tornista korkein, ja sen valmistuminen nostaa kirkon täyteen 172,5 metrin korkeuteensa.

## Symbolinen hetki Gaudín merkkivuonna

Siunaus järjestettiin 10. kesäkuuta, Antoni Gaudín kuoleman satavuotispäivänä. Gaudín suunnittelema Sagrada Família on yksi Barcelonan tunnetuimmista rakennuksista ja modernistisen arkkitehtuurin maamerkeistä. Rakennustyöt alkoivat paikalla 144 vuotta sitten.

Tilaisuudessa oli mukana Espanjan kuningaspari, Espanjan pääministeri Pedro Sánchez sekä satoja piispoja. Paikalle kerääntyi myös suuri yleisö, ja tilaisuutta seurattiin suoratoistona sekä Sagrada Famílian verkkosivustolla että TikTokissa. Lähteiden mukaan paavin eteen kokoontui yli 8 000 ihmistä.

## Maailman korkein kirkko

Jeesuksen Kristuksen torni valmistui helmikuussa. Sen myötä Sagrada Família saavutti täyden korkeutensa ja sai aseman maailman korkeimpana kirkkona. Samalla rakennuksesta tuli myös Barcelonan korkein rakennus. Lähteissä korkeudeksi mainitaan 172,5 metriä, eli 566 jalkaa.

Uuden tornin siunausta on kuvattu historialliseksi hetkeksi basilikan pitkällä rakennusurakalla. Kirkko vihittiin käyttöön vuonna 2010 paavi Benedictus XVI:n toimittamassa konsekratiossa, mutta nyt siunattu torni merkitsee yhden keskeisen rakennusvaiheen valmistumista.

## Keskustelu suunnitelmista jatkuu

Vaikka tornin siunaus merkitsee suurta askelta kohti kokonaisuuden valmistumista, basilikan ympärillä käydään yhä keskustelua siitä, kuinka tarkasti nykyinen rakennus vastaa Gaudín alkuperäisiä suunnitelmia. Kysymys on noussut esiin erityisesti siksi, että Sagrada Famíliaa on rakennettu sukupolvien ajan arkkitehdin kuoleman jälkeen.

Seremonia korosti sekä rakennuksen uskonnollista merkitystä että sen asemaa yhtenä Euroopan tunnetuimmista kulttuurikohteista. Paavin vierailu, Espanjan valtiojohdon läsnäolo ja suuri yleisö tekivät tornin siunauksesta näkyvän päätöskohdan yhdelle basilikan pitkän historian tärkeimmistä vaiheista.
